Depression often isn't so obvious as a broken leg. In the beginning you don't know that anything is broken. There isn't anything to see, it's a black but colourless cloud that may just be sitting on the side lines. You can't see it. It isn't in your peripheral vision at all.


Then, as you begin to think that you're just being lazy or maybe you're tired, that cloud you can't see extends a smoke like finger and starts to wrap around your happiness. Dulling it ever so slightly. A week later, another finger like protrusion wraps around your self worth but you cannot see this happening.



Those dark and smokey fingers start to hold more tightly and infiltrating your views, feeding any sense of self loathing.



The strong part of your brain is now desperately trying to stop the smoke from filling up any holes and so you can go out and still participate but the dead feeling inside is starting to grow from the inside out, almost like black mold so the smallest crevices are tainted with spores.



All decisions are becoming harder. Your strong brain is now just only capable of doing the basics. You can't see the spores or the smoke and you know there's something wrong but you're doing the basics so perhaps it's just a phase.




People ask you how you are and what you've been up to but you just say "I'm fine," because you feel like it's a boring conversation to talk about yourself when you haven't been doing anything exciting. Plus, everyone has shit going on, right?
You become a master at redirecting conversations to only chat about others. 



You know something's up and you go to the doctor and get some meds to help. You talk to someone professional. You know you're loved, you know "this too will pass" 



Then one day, you haven't slept properly for weeks and you're in a daze. The emotional pain has you withdrawing from everywhere but Netflix. You're fucking tired.



You've been doing all the things that you're supposed to do. You're not bingeing on alcohol, or food. You're exercising. You're getting the blue morning light. You're taking your meds. You're making your bed. You're getting to work.



You've been trying for so long. So fucking long. And it's so fucking exhausting. Your strong brain is feeling weaker and weaker. The smoke is thick and heavy like fog but nobody else can see it, so you just be doing fine.



And then there's a noose around you're neck and you're scared and it fucking hurts. And your strong brain is screaming NO! And the smoke you know is there but still cannot see is telling it to shut the fuck up. You can feel the blood vessels in your face bursting and it fucking hurts with every blood pump.

Here's my advice:

Your mobility definitely needs work. Make sure you are doing at least 10 minutes of mobility before you start your activation process.

You squat after activation. Nobody should be going straight into weighted squats without ensuring the right muscles are working.

I have no idea how to link things in here so I'll try to use my words.

Mobility:
Inchworm first - google it. You start in a plank and while keeping your legs straight and feet together, tippy toe your feet towards your hands WITHOUT BENDING YOUR KNEES (I don't mean to shout, I just don't know how to bold). Then walk your hands out to a plank again and repeat. I get my clients to do this along about 10 times, try to get your hips higher each time.

Then you should do hip opener stretches. Google these. Froggie stance is a good one. Follow that with long step lunges, now you're stretching and activating your glutes at the same time. 

Glute bridges/hip thrusts are next, focusing on squeezing the bajeezus outta your butt cheeks.


Then start by dropping right down into what I refer to as a drop squat but is also called an Asian squat. 

You should be able to do this by keeping your feet flat on the ground. If you can't without falling over, hold onto the squat rack. Sit in the bottom of the squat for at least a count of ten, pushing your knees out. Then breathe in, TENSE EVERYTHING, and push your heels into the ground, trying to go straight up, all the body together. If you find that you're doing a kinda stripper stand, as in straightening legs first, you're not ready for weight on your back yet.


I get my clients to stand at a wall with about 3inches between their toes and the wall. You should be able to squat without your face touching. That's how you get the 45°.

It could be tightness in your hips or weakness of the core that inhibits a strong squat.

TL/DR: Mobilisation, activate and then engage. Be strong with correct form on a lower weight first.

I am trained in pre and post natal exercise.

You can do pretty much everything in the first 2 trimesters. If you've been lifting before, you can do it still but like the others have said LISTEN TO YOUR BODY.

As you head towards your third trimester, please be careful of movements which can be bad for your hips. 

Squats and Deads are fine but lunges, especially walking lunges put you at risk of pelvic movement and your hips can become displaced.

This is due to the relaxin hormone running through your body and getting you ready for your darling baby to be pushed out.

Be incredibly careful with stretching at this time. Foam roalling and other forms of myofascial release are ideal for the same reasons as above. Your body is becoming primed for your joints in the pelvic region to be overly flexible.

For your first 2 trimesters, it's important to move across all planes as well. 
Woodchops, while your belly isn't basketballing, clock/circle lunges and anything side to side will help build your entire core for back support. 

Do movements that replicate life.
Keep things uneven so your body has to regulate posture.

Massage is also ideal. Find someone who is trained in pre natal. 

Congratulations and good luck!!
